subject: Execution locus, transfer pathways, and deletion assurances - prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion guarantees

Hi Jordan,

Quick follow-up from our legal/security intake — before we move to an eval, can you confirm a few things about runtime geography and deletion? High level asks below:

1) When a user from our EU tenant calls your hosted API, where does the model actually execute (region/hop list)?
2) Which subprocessors might touch request metadata or logs during routing and training-prep steps?
3) If we ask for immediate deletion of a dataset / conversation, what is the expected end-to-end timeline and what controls do we have (API, KMS, retention windows)?

We don’t need any legal docs yet; just an operational summary and any evidence artifacts you can share (diagram, subproc list).

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Security Operations
Nimbus Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion guarantees

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. I put together an operational summary below and attached a current subprocessor inventory and a simple execution diagram. High-level answers:

1) Execution locus: by default, requests from EU customers are routed to our EU region (Frankfurt) for model execution. We operate regional inference clusters (EU, US-West, US-East, APAC) and prefer single-region execution when a regional route is available. If capacity is constrained we have policy-driven fallbacks to nearby regions (EU -> US-East) — routing rules and fallbacks are configurable per account.

2) Subprocessors: the actual GPU execution is on instances we manage in customer-dedicated pools or our hosted fleet. Network/load routing and observability may involve cloud providers (AWS eu-central-1, GCP europe-west1) and edge CDN/cache providers for static assets. The attached PDF lists subprocessors and their roles; primary categories: compute (hosted VMs/GPU), networking (VPC transit, CDN), logging/monitoring (aggregated metrics), and DLP/evidence storage (for audit packets).

3) Deletion timeline & controls: we provide a Deletion API that queues a deletion job and purges model-level KV/prefix caches within minutes. For persistent logs/analytics and backups, typical SLA is 30 days to fully purge from warm storage, and 90 days for deep archival removal depending on retention policies you select. If you require accelerated deletion we can set a contract-side commitment and use dedicated deletion workflows; for GDPR-erasures we support a documented DPA flow and can provide attestations.

I’ve attached: redwood_subprocessors_20280503.pdf and a simple geo-transfer-diagram.png. Monica — looping you for any clarifications on provable deletion and customer KMS options.

Next step: if this level looks ok, I can coordinate a short tech walkthrough with your infra team to show routing rules and deletion demo.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@nimbushealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 May 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where requests are executed and deletion guarantees

Hi Elena — quick technical addendum from the infra team (pasted below). For your review and to make sure we’re answering precisely for Nimbus’ compliance controls.

On request routing and hops:
- Ingress: API front door is regional and resolves by customer-configured routing policy. IP ingress terminates in the regional load balancer.
- Execution: Model inference occurs inside the region on Redwood-managed GPU nodes. We maintain a short-lived ephemeral KV cache per-request; persistent KV caches are region-scoped.
- Cross-border fallbacks: when fallbacks trigger we perform encrypted transfer over TLS 1.3 between regions. Transfers are logged; we can enable reduced logging for sensitive tenants (log redaction).

On subprocessors & evidence:
- Subprocessors may see metadata (timestamps, region tags, anonymized request IDs) but not plaintext inputs when Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK) are enabled.
- We publish the full subprocessor list and will provide signed attestations for the subprocessors that handle routing and storage.

On deletion mechanics and SLA:
- Customer Deletion API: 1) deletion request accepted and returns job id, 2) removal from active KV/prefix caches: typically <5 minutes, 3) removal from warm storage (logs/analytics): configurable 7–30 days, 4) archival purge (if enabled): up to 90 days.
- Accelerated erasure: available for enterprise contracts; can commit to 7-day full purge with dedicated workflows.
- For EU customers we support SCCs and our DPA includes subprocessors list and retention windows.

Dev — attaching a short Word extract of the SCC-relevant execution clauses (scc-execution-extract.docx).

If you want, we can produce a short evidence pack (signed subproc list + network flow diagram + deletion log sample) for your security review.

—Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
